claim_text: In In Timaeum 142 Calcidius opens a sustained dispute over fate, will and mixed positions; 143 states that according to Plato providence precedes fate; 144 reports Chrysippus and Cleanthes on the relation of fate to providence; 145 distinguishes providence, decree/fate, what occurs from our will, fortune and chance; 146 says the secondary gods' divine command is the perpetual order called fate and derives from providence.

locator.edition_or_witness: Johann Wrobel (ed.), Platonis Timaeus interprete Chalcidio cum eiusdem commentario (Teubner 1876), checked CHMTL transcription

notes: Independently verified at this five-section scope after correcting stale counts, false Plato authorship edges and school metadata. It does not establish a complete Calcidius doctrine, source genealogy, religious identity or exact school membership.
